question.text: Twenty people were executed for being associated with the Devil during these series of hearings. Arthur Miller wrote about these events in The Crucible.
question.clue: They started after doctor William Griggs provided treatment for certain hysterical fits, and "spectral evidence" during these events was allowed by Cotton Mather.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Spanish Florida.
swap.text: The Spanish founded this city in Florida in 1565, making it America's oldest city.
swap.clue: The 1763 Treaty of Paris ceded this city's colony, against which James Oglethorpe led a 1740 expedition.

question.leadin: The Battle of Jumonville Glen began this war, after which British colonial forces retreated to Fort Necessity.
question.text: Identify this war, named for the two forces allied against British and colonial troops. This conflict was part of the larger Seven Years' War.
question.clue: A namesake expedition in this conflict was ambushed at the Monongahela River by forces under Daniel Beaujeu, leading to the death of General Braddock.

swap.text: While the route he took is under debate, this man was the first European to cross the Mississippi River, on whose banks he would perish due to fever.
swap.clue: After he died of illness, his mission was continued by Luis de Moscoso Alvarado.

question.leadin: Everyone likes pirates! Answer these questions about real pirates.
question.text: In 1718, this man blockaded the port of Charlestown with his ship The Queen Anne's Revenge and two smaller vessels. He allegedly lit fuses around his face to appear more menacing.
question.clue: This man used the wealth gained from rogue toll operations in Pamlico Sound to purchase protection from Charles Eden of North Carolina and eventually redubbed the Concorde the Royal James after earlier flying it under the moniker Queen Anne's Revenge.

swap.leadin: In this conflict, Governor William Berkeley "bared his breast" and challenged this event's namesake leader to shoot him.
swap.text: Name this 1676 conflict in which frontier-dwelling colonists forcibly demanded that the governor protect them against the Native American threat.
swap.clue: AnnCotton described this event in a letter titled "An account of our late troubles in" the colony whereit tookplace.

question.leadin: This time period was aggravated by the crashing of the Sea Venture in Bermuda and the loss of effective leadership when John Smith departed.
question.text: Name this season which only sixty people survived in the affected area. It ended when Thomas West, Baron De la Warr brought ships full of supplies and John Rolfe introduced tobacco planting.
question.answerHtml: the “starving time” [or the winter from 1609 to 1610; or the winter from 1609 to 1610; prompt “1609;” prompt “1610”]
question.clue: A major cause of this period, during which some relief came from trade with the Nansemonds, was the failure of the Third Supply due to the wreck of the Sea Venture, an event which inspired The Tempest.

swap.text: This Quaker founded a colony named for him in 1681, from which Delaware later split off.
swap.clue: Before traveling overseas aboard the Welcome, he helped author the Concessions and Agreements Charter and prepared an early democratic constitution for his territory in his First Frame of Government.

question.leadin: Name these founders of early American colonies.
question.text: In 1732, this English philanthropist received a charter from George II to settle the colony of Georgia, making it not only a buffer against Spanish invasion but also a refuge for debtors.
question.clue: Earlier, this man led a Parliamentary committee on prison reform, which inspired him to found a haven for debtors.

swap.leadin: Its first assembly was presided over by George Yeardley, who had earlier participated in the ill-fated Third Supply Mission.
swap.text: Name this legislative body, the first such body in the British Colonies. White landowning men over 17 had the right to vote in members, and in 1699 it was moved to Williamsburg.
swap.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

question.leadin: This man founded Fort Christina and was the first governor of New Sweden.
question.text: Name this Dutchman who had earlier purchased the island of Manhattan from Native Americans for goods worth sixty guilders, or twenty-four dollars.
question.clue: This man was then financed by Samuel Blommaert to sail aboard the Kalmar Nyckel, which he landed at a tributary called the Minquas Kill.

swap.leadin: This man was taught English by Ferdinando Gorges.
swap.text: Name this member of the Patuxet tribe, who taught a group of early American settlers how to catch eels and farm corn using a fertilizer called menhaden.
swap.clue: This man was taken prisoner and almost executed by Corbitant, as recorded in Mourt's Relation.

question.leadin: This politician suspended the New York legislature after it refused to recognize the Quartering Act.
question.text: Identify this British politician whose set of namesake acts spurred the non-importation movement in the colonies.
question.clue: A series of five acts named for this man aimed to enforce the Quartering Act in New York and to save the British East India Company. The placement of British troops in Boston due to those acts eventually led to the Boston Massacre.

swap.leadin: This tribe developed a voting procedure where a corn kernel meant agreement, while a pea meant opposition.
swap.text: Name this matrilineal tribe that signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation with the English. This tribe's Queen Cockacoeske was succeeded by Queens Betty and Ann, who may have been the same person.
swap.clue: This tribe's female chief Cockacoeske was killed during Bacon's Rebellion. Powhatan and his daughter Pocahontas belonged to this tribe.

question.text: This Puritan poet wrote of the "pettish wasp" in "Upon a Spider Catching a Fly," and asked "make me, O Lord, thy Spinning Wheel complete" in "Huswifery."

swap.leadin: An academy that seeks to preserve this language has forty members who are nicknamed "Immortals."
swap.text: Name this language that replaced Latin as the chief diplomatic language in Europe starting in the 17th century and lasting until the end of World War I.
swap.clue: A 1768 rebellion, sometimes named for people who primarily spoke this language, forced governor Antonio de Ulloa ("oo-YOH-ah") out of power.

question.leadin: This two-word phrase was coined by Edmund Burke in his "Speech for the Conciliation with the Colonies."
question.text: Name this phrase ofen used to describe Prime Minister Robert Walpole's unofcial policy of declining to enforce strict Parliamentary laws on the American colonies, such as trade and religion laws, so as to allow the colonies to fourish.
question.clue: This name for the policy of non-interference and lax oversight in the relationship between England and the American colonies in the 17th and early 18th century.

swap.leadin: Chiefs Blount and Hancock led opposing factions of this nation, whose name in their native language means "hemp gatherers" or "shirt-wearing people."
swap.text: Name this tribe which fought a 1711-15 civil war in North Carolina, complete with outside intervention from the British, German, Dutch, Yamasee, and Cherokee.
swap.clue: They threatened to take sides in the struggle between Thomas Cary and Governor Hyde, and ultimately formed alliances with the Nynee and Bear River peoples to prosecute an unsuccessful 1711 to 1713 war against North Carolina.

question.text: As a teenager, Franklin published a series of letters in the New-England Courant using this feminine surname.
question.clue: As an apprentice, Benjamin Franklin printed the New-England Courant newspaper, which featured this female persona of his giving humorous accounts of colonial life.

swap.leadin: Johan Campanius Holm, a pastor from this colony, provided the first translation of a Christian catechism into a Native American language when he translated Luther's Small Catechism into Unami.
swap.text: Name this colony established by a namesake company with the foundation of a fort on the Christina River, after Peter Minuit led the ships Kalmar Nyckel and Vogel Grip from Scandinavia into Delaware Bay in 1638.
swap.clue: Like New Netherland, which eventually conquered it, it was founded by an expedition led by Peter Minuit.
